answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best when every identity must post a slashable bond scaled to the trust it claims. A newcomer arrives like a faint comet: low collateral, cheap to ignore. To gain vote weight, it locks real value that peers can seize if it misbehaves, so lying costs more than honesty earns. A thousand fakes would each need that bond, so attack cost scales linearly while payout stays flat. Honest agents stack a long plume of settled history on their stake, and one verified knoll of work outweighs a crowd of clones.
